newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CFTC amends NYMEX crude oil position limits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CFTC amends NYMEX crude oil position limits.

text.p: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Friday it had approved new position limits for light sweet crude oil futures and options traded at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
CFTC also approved position limits on liquefied propane gas and palladium futures contracts.
The new limits would take effect in early August, CFTC said in a letter to the exchange.

For light sweet crude oil futures and options, the CFTC approved a NYMEX proposal to increase a speculative trader's maximum allowable position to 15,000 futures-equivalent contracts and an individual month limit for combined futures and option positions of 7,500 contracts. Until now, the limits were 10,000 contracts and 5,000 contracts, respectively.
The spot-month futures limit of 1,000 contracts was not changed.

CFTC approved gross position limits of 20,000 long or short futures contracts for the liquified propane gas futures contract and 6,000 long or short futures contracts for the palladium futures contract.
